case_title: Kavita Chandrakant Lakhani v. State of Maharashtra & Anr.
accused_victim_relationship: Prior intimate relationship (acquaintance/partner); relationship known to both families
statutory_provisions: IPC s.366 (discharge sought; not maintainable); charge sheet under ss.363, 342, 324, 354, 323, 506(II); charges framed 13.06.2012 under ss.342, 324, 323, 354
evidence_type: Eyewitness (watchman); complainant's testimony/statements (FIR and later supplementary statement)
trial_court_outcome: Sessions Judge discharged accused of s.366 (also 363 and 506(ii)) on 04.07.2007; the earlier ACMM order of 03.10.2006 had refused discharge and committed the case
high_court_outcome: Criminal Writ Petition No. 3766 of 2012 dismissed on 06.05.2013 (discharge order upheld)
neutral_facts: The victim and the accused had been in a relationship known to both families. After a birthday party attended by both and their friends, the accused offered to drop the victim at a venue for dinner but instead drove the victim to the accused's home. When the victim refused to leave the car, the accused pulled the victim out forcibly, carried the victim into the house and placed the victim on a bed. According to the victim, the accused first declared love and asked why the victim was not marrying the accused, then beat the victim with the hands and a waist belt and struck the victim's head against a wall, causing injuries. A watchman witnessed the victim being pulled from the car. At about 2 a.m. the accused's father returned home and the victim was taken home. A complaint was lodged on 12 September 2003 describing these acts. A week later, on 19 September 2003, a further statement added allegations that the accused removed the victim's clothes and touched the victim inappropriately. The victim explained the omission by embarrassment. A charge sheet was filed on 30 March 2004 under sections of the Penal Code covering abduction, wrongful confinement, hurt, outraging modesty and criminal intimidation.
offence_severity: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine (s.366); minimum not stated
physical_harm: Injuries to the victim from beating with hands and belt and head striking wall (extent not stated)
number_of_offences: 6 charged (ss.363, 342, 324, 354, 323, 506(II)) plus s.366 discharge sought; 0 finally upheld (no conviction; trial pending)
premeditation_planning: No; court found no proven intent to marry or seduce; later version an afterthought
motive: alleged: sudden outbreak of emotions or sense of insecurity (court's tentative view only; not decided)
key_evidence_accepted: Primary allegations in the complainant's FIR: forcible taking to accused's house, expressions of love, beating; watchman's account of pulling victim from car
witness_credibility: Victim's later molestation account not believed: delay and unexplained omission made it an afterthought; primary allegations accepted as evident on record
trial_duration: offence: 06/07.09.2003; trial judgment: not given (committal order 03.10.2006; Sessions discharge order 04.07.2007); High Court: 06.05.2013; Supreme Court: 24.04.2018
legal_representation: Appellant (complainant): Siddharth Luthra, Sr. Adv. with others. Respondent No. 2 (accused): Mahesh Jethmalani, Sr. Adv. with others. State: Nishant R. Katneshwarkar, counsel for the respondent-State
investigation_status: FIR No. 247 of 2003 registered 12.09.2003; charge sheet filed 30.03.2004; charges framed 13.06.2012; trial not concluded
procedural_irregularity: Long delay: matter pending since 2003 and still at charge-framing stage
appeal_history: Trial court (Sessions Judge, 04.07.2007): accused discharged of s.366. High Court (06.05.2013): writ petition dismissed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Appellant (complainant) argued that the complaint and supplementary statement, read together, disclose s.366, s.363 and s.506(ii) offences; relied on Cref Finance
defence_argument: Accused argued the complaint did not mention ss.366, 363 or 506(ii); later supplementary statement was an afterthought; relied on Dharam Pal
legal_principle_applied: For s.366, abduction alone is insufficient; prosecution must prove abduction with intent to compel marriage or force/seduce to illicit intercourse
precedent_relied_upon: Cref Finance Ltd. v. Shree Shanthi Homes (P) Ltd. (2005) 7 SCC 467 (held inapplicable); Dharam Pal v. State of Haryana (2014) 3 SCC 306 (held inapplicable)
other_sentence_order: Direction to trial court to conclude trial within 6 months from the judgment; observations limited to s.366 applicability

case_title.quote: KAVITA CHANDRAKANT LAKHANI v. STATE OF MAHARASHTRA & ANR.

number_of_accused.quote: Respondent no.2 discharged inter alia in respect of offence u/s.366

accused_gender.quote: Respondent No. 2 forcibly lifted her up and took her to his house and put her on bed

victim_gender.quote: Respondent No. 2 forcibly lifted her up and took her to his house and put her on bed

accused_victim_relationship.quote: It is evident on record that Respondent No. 2 and the appellant herein were in a relationship which was known to their families also.

offence_category.quote: This Court has time and again held that mere abduction does not bring an accused under the ambit of Section 366 IPC.

statutory_provisions.quote: A charge sheet in the case was filed on 30.03.2004 before the Court of Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, 40 th Court

weapon.quote: started beating her with waist belt and using his hands which fact is evident on record

evidence_type.quote: The act of pulling out the appellant herein from the car of Respondent No. 2 was witnessed by the watchman.

trial_court_outcome.quote: learned Judge, Sessions Court, vide order dated 04.07.2007 had discharged the Respondent No. 2 not only in respect of offence under Section 366 of the IPC

high_court_outcome.quote: learned single Judge of the High Court dismissed the petition filed by Kavita Chandrakant Lakhani

final_outcome.quote: We are in agreement with the order passed by the High Court.

neutral_facts.quote: As per the allegations in the complaint, in the early hours of 07.09.2003, when all the friends proceeded towards the venue for dinner, Respondent No. 2 herein, in order to drop her to the venue, took her to his house

offence_severity.quote: shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extent do ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

attempt_completion.quote: Even if it is proved that Respondent No. 2 forcibly took her to his house

physical_harm.quote: As a result, she sustained injuries on her person.

number_of_offences.quote: Learned ACMM, vide order dated 03.10.2006, rejected the discharge application and committed the case

premeditation_planning.quote: The very same acts of Respondent No. 2 do not show his intent to abduct her in order to marry her against her will

motive.quote: A t the highest, the case can be put that both of them were in a relationship and due to sudden outbreak of emotions or due to sense of insecurity on the part of Respondent No. 2, the above act was done.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: Actually, as per the prosecutrix, Respondent No. 2 first expressed his love for her and afterwards he started beating her with waist belt and using his hands which fact is evident on record.

witness_credibility.quote: This does not inspire confidence as the FIR was lodged by appellant, five days after the incident, with due deliberation

trial_duration.quote: The incident took place on 06/07.09.2003 and FIR got registered on 12.09.2003

legal_representation.quote: Siddharth Luthra, Sr. Adv., Robin Jaisinghani, Vikas Mehta, Vijay Gandhi, Samir Chaudhary, Ms. Purnima Raj, Ms. Anushree Menon, Advs. for the Appellant.

investigation_status.quote: A First Information Report (FIR) bearing No. 247 of 2003 PS Gamdevi, District Mumbai dated 12.09.2003 was got registered

procedural_irregularity.quote: since the matter is pending since 2003 and is still at the stage of charge framing, we deem it appropriate to direct the trial Court to conclude the trial within 6 (months)

appeal_history.quote: learned single Judge of the High Court, vide order dated 06.05.2013, dismissed the writ petition filed by the appellant.

prosecution_argument.quote: if the complaint and the supplementary statement is taken in its true perspective, no case has been made out for the discharge of Respondent No. 2

defence_argument.quote: the supplementary statement given by the appellant after about 5 (five) months is only an afterthought just to implicate Respondent No. 2

legal_principle_applied.quote: mere finding that a woman was abducted is not enough, it must further be proved that the accused abducted the woman with the intent that she may be compelled

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Cref Finance Ltd. v. Shree Shanthi Homes (P) Ltd. and Another (2005) 7 SCC 467

other_sentence_order.quote: we deem it appropriate to direct the trial Court to conclude the trial within 6 (months) from the date of passing of this judgment
